An honest release boundary

Built. Tested.
Not finished.

Passing functional checks are not a 60 FPS badge. These captures use software graphics, not a Radeon 840M laptop.

  • The reported lag is not solved. Actual two-minute populated software observations are 1.859 FPS Balanced / 2.461 FPS Auto, despite adaptive reduction. The final population-off diagnostics are also slow. Native near60, ten nearby cars and the historical ≤8 ms streaming gate remain unaccepted.
  • City art is still a prototype. Repetitive far buildings, sparse blocks, LOD noise and steep-road blending remain visible. A full-map stall-free flight is not proven.
  • GitHub exists; the push is pending. The private sarang-cmd/crosstown repository was created with ten topics. Secure authentication for the source push is unavailable; no hosted CI pass is claimed.
  • Fairness, feel and realism need review. Long traffic queues leave strict no-stuck acceptance open; clean samples are not exhaustive proof. No by-ear mix or physical wheel/rumble sign-off. Social alignment and final art need work; police, weapons and deep radio are future scope.
01 / Controls & commitment

A means left. D means right.

Corrected the keyboard camera-space basis, removed yaw feedback, added damped follow/look and retained collision sweeps. Quick / Standard / Full replace the sole long-run commitment.

02 / Feature-preserving work

Twelve vehicles. Six spaces.

Twelve independent glTF exteriors and physical tunings, six matching cabins and 96 roster engine loops. Damage, paint and a six-car garage extend the retained ignition, four views, fallback audio and real mirror pixels.

03 / Public verification

Checked outside the dev server.

99 units and 25 selected browser cases pass, plus a separate public-car smoke. All 189 anonymous public files match, also after temporary transfer shutdown. Real wall-time watches, accelerated soaks and software profiles are separate. Native 60 FPS and strict no-stuck remain open.
